result.root_cause: extractFile writes a zip entry to a path built from attacker-controlled entry names without verifying the resolved file stays within the destination directory, allowing `../` traversal (Zip Slip) outside the target.
result.summary: Our patch places a containment guard at the exact sink (extractFile) that every taint trace flows through, canonicalizing both the destination dir and the resolved file and rejecting any entry that escapes. It is semantically equivalent to the official fix but strictly stronger: getCanonicalPath resolves symlinks and `..`, and appending File.separator prevents the sibling-prefix bypass (e.g. /out vs /out-evil) that the official getAbsolutePath().startsWith() check would miss. Normal extraction is preserved. The only caveat is that the pipeline did not empirically run the POV-before or regressions, so efficacy is established by code analysis rather than execution.
